name: On-site gas turbine power generation
applications: island and parallel operation with the grid
principle: Facilities generate their own power with gas turbine generator sets when the grid is weak, absent or considered unreliable, or when waste heat from exhaust can drive steam for process use (cogeneration). Industrial and aeroderivative turbines from about 5 MW to well above 100 MW are installed per train; multiple units run with a power management system, spinning reserve and load-shed logic. Offshore and remote platforms historically ran at 4.16 kV or 11 kV with closed-bus transfer between boards.

process_steps.name: Fuel burns in combustors; turbine expands hot gas
Generator converts shaft power to electricity
Exhaust heat raised to steam where cogeneration applies
PMS dispatches generation against demand, reserve and shed priority

limitations: fuel is a large fixed opex; efficiency of simple-cycle industrial sets is far below combined cycle
island operation demands careful transient studies, load-shed tuning and closed-bus transfer design
advantages: energy independence for remote sites and platforms
exhaust heat reuse makes cogeneration efficiency attractive versus grid plus boilers
